## 2026-11-19 - Fable senior: score-term audit + Gate A crossover-loading diagnosis (CPU only, committed)

- **Verdict.** The "650-900 Hz loading hump" reported earlier today was unit-acceleration referencing, not acoustics.
  - The solver drives unit normal acceleration (`meta.spl_reference`).
  - Per unit velocity, fold_warm 00826f071b24 is +1.3/+2.8 dB of power at 643/828 Hz relative to 2 kHz. That equals 10 log10 of its Re z ratio (1.93/1.03).
  - Balloon power over throat input power is 0.95-1.00 for all six audit designs on both grids.
  - The feature is one near-cutoff Re z overshoot, not a resonance train.
  - rosse_rect_cd and tritonia_v9 are 5-8 dB under-loaded at 643-828 Hz, so `load` charges a real deficit.
  - The real ripple is ext_throat a23763f1c6fc: Re z 0.59 at 1.2-1.4 kHz.
- **Driver-independent.** The ranking holds for all 32 members of an [inferred] 1.4"-exit driver bracket.
  - The owner has said the driver is open; it need not be the HF1440.
  - No 1.4" pro driver checked publishes Mmd, Sd or fs.
- **Score policy.** v10 and `dislope` are unchanged, and no v11 is justified.
  - dislope = 0 promotes beaming horns (audit F1). Side lobes (F3) and max_edge (F4) were rejected.
  - Screen->verify floor: `load` explains 56% of the variance. The directivity sub-J SD is 0.055 J on the top-28. That is a grid sensitivity, not a confidence interval.
  - Audit decision 3 (the hold on J-only continuations) is lifted. Decision 2 (no B6 reruns on the current grid) stands.
- **Code.**
  - New `tools/analysis/xo_loading_report.py`, report-only XO diagnostics. 6 tests, including a pulsating-sphere energy-balance check.
  - `tools/analysis/rescore_identity.py` rows now also carry `run_path` (audit F8: 35 nested rows had stored only `screen`). `run` is unchanged.
  - 19 targeted tests pass.
- **Evidence.**
  - Reproducible outputs: `docs/evidence/xo_loading_gateA_2026-11-19/`.
  - Reports and scripts, force-added under `scratch/fable_architecture/`: `score_term_audit_2026-11-19/` (F6 banner-corrected) and `xo_loading_gateA_2026-11-19/`.
- **Provenance.** 205 hashes have more than one design dir. 9 of them are on different meshes (up to 0.21 dB), so the same hash is not the same field.
- **Not done (owner-gated).** Optional dense re-solve: 3 designs, 1/24 oct, 450-1800 Hz, `HORNLAB_GPU_LOCK=refuse`. No GPU, queue, default or score identity was touched. Unrelated uncommitted GUI edits in the tree were left alone.

## 2026-11-18 - Near-throat H/V control: audit, research (KH-002), option literature (KH-003)

- Docs only; no code. Root cause in OS generators: `a0` (from `driver.exit_angle_deg`) and `k`
  are shared by every azimuth, so only `a(phi)` splits H/V, and that split grows late. The
  `throat_ext_length_mm` extension is round (search pressure pins it short). The rolled and
  toroidal routes have no near-throat H/V term.
- Primary-verified: Batík OS-SE allows its parameters to vary around the device, so a per-azimuth
  `a0`/`k` stays inside the OS-SE parent. R-OSSE is unclassified. Smoothstep section ramps and
  OS-SE plus elliptical throat extensions are labeled hybrids.
- Proposed (owner approval pending): one shared throat H/V block (asymmetry ratio, onset fraction,

  `scratch/sigma_out2.txt`): refusal storms track sigma0 × free-keys × bound width (0.22–0.25 on

  azimuths = 3° step), inner-wall mesh agreement passes ext-throat (10/10, worst p99 0.158 mm), ATH
  morph (10/10, 0.850) and biradial (10/10, 0.142), but fails rolled (0/10, 1.696) and Crowe

  0.36–0.59) and 65 stations are sufficient; 31 azimuths aliases the relief. Crowe's native
  25 × 41 point grid already sits at p99 1.07 mm from the stored mesh (mesher surface fit, not

## 2026-11-16 - Agent-orchestration review: sessions are slow because of prompt size, not agent count

- Review filed at [`AGENT_ORCHESTRATION_REVIEW_2026-11-16.md`](AGENT_ORCHESTRATION_REVIEW_2026-11-16.md).
  Docs-only: no code, config, prompt, queue or GPU change; **nothing applied**. Trigger was the
  owner's report of agents running long, spawning too many subagents, and re-briefing them instead
  of continuing them.
- Measured from the local OpenCode telemetry DB (7 days, read-only): 58 root sessions and 191 child
  sessions; 206 `task` calls against 40 `task_revive` in 30 days (~93 % cold starts); children
  average 111k input tokens to re-onboard (fixer 122k, designer 143k; 21.2M total); weekly spend
  $61.73 ($43.04 root, $18.69 child).
- Root cause, ranked. (1) **53 of 58 root sessions, and 241 of the 244 steps with >600k-token
  prompts, were launched from `C:/Users/hunte/Hrns`** - the container directory, which has no
  `AGENTS.md` and no skill grants, so sessions explore the worktrees and forks blind. (2) The
  documented reading order points at `docs/CONTINUITY.md` (844,727 B / 5,930 lines / 390 entries)
  with no read budget, plus `ISSUES.md` 407,673 B and `NOTES_FOR_SENIOR.md` 125,130 B; 42.6 % of
  the 16,887 measured steps ran above 200k prompt tokens, 11.3 % above 400k, max 832k. (3) A
  standing 4-7 lane fan-out ("Lane A-G") rather than occasional parallelism. (4) rbassist-only
  prompt blocks sit in the globally scoped `orchestrator_append.md` (~950 tokens on every Hornlab
  turn), and `skills: ["*"]` resolves to rbassist skills because the eight HornLab skills live in
  `hornlab-search/.claude/skills`.
- Proposed and deliberately **not applied** (each with mechanism, risk and validation in the
  report): container `Hrns/AGENTS.md` (P0-1); reading-budget amendment to `AGENTS.md` (P0-2);
  rbassist prompt blocks moved to rbassist project scope (P1-1); dispatch rewrite with a 3-lane cap
  and a <=2-file direct-work threshold (P1-2); preset retier - orchestrator `max`->`high`, `oracle`
  off `glm-5.3-flash`, fixer->`medium` (P2-1); concurrency 6->4 (P2-2).
- Decisions still needed before any of it is implemented are listed in section 7 of the report
  (8 items, including the single cost increase: the `oracle` tier).
- Method caveat: session wall-clock durations in the DB are **not** runtime (several root sessions
  were reopened across days and read 294-491 h). The review measures step prompt size, not session
  duration, and does not project a percentage speed-up.

## 2026-11-16 - V2A timing-law endpoint correction (CPU geometry only)

- The V2A timing law `smootherstep(u/a)/smootherstep(1/a)` did not guarantee zero first/second
  derivatives at the mouth unless u50=0.5 (measured |dS/du| about 1.087 at u50=0.65). Replaced with
  the warped quintic `q=u50/(1-u50)`, `w=u/(u+q(1-u))`, `S=smootherstep(w)`, which keeps the single
  u50 coordinate and gives S(0)=0, S(u50)=0.5, S(1)=1, S'=S''=0 at both ends for every u50.
- Added analytic `timing_derivatives()` and tests at u50=0.35/0.50/0.65 plus the fixed 20 mm hold
  (raw half point 0.464286); endpoint S'/S'' are 0 within 1e-12.
- Regenerated evidence: c0 cuts unchanged (u50=0.5); c2 40/60 mm values updated; T2 practical rank
  remains 4 at three parents (max |cosine| 0.640); 8 kHz mesh unchanged at 8,318 tris, 0 bad open
  edges, driven plane 36.000x36.000 mm. 18 V2A tests green (one config-load test is blocked only by
  the concurrent uncommitted v9 objective registration, not by this change).
- No solve, GPU, queue or objective change.

## 2026-11-16 (23:25) - A study lists its solves and renders any measured design in 3D on demand

- Owner decision: a Bayesian study is inspectable like a run - the same solve list and the same
  best-solve plots - while its Bayesian identity (policy, engine, model/diagnostics) stays separate.
  Mechanism: an **on-demand verify job** per design. No change to `studies/**`, no code-pin change.
- `data.solves` (execute + decide phases): one row per observed attempt with an identity - design
  hash, kind, J, physical, outcome, physical coverage/ripple, params/descriptors - 50 max, J
  ascending, with `n_total`/`n_measured`/`n_refused`/`truncated`. Coverage/ripple come only from a
  physical source (normalized terms are never shown as degrees/dB); a `verify_run_id` comes only from
  the solve ledger and only while that run folder still exists.
- `solve_design` job (`gui/study_jobs.py`, GPU): writes a real standalone verify run
  `runs/<utc-ts>-studyverify-<hash6>` (config snapshot, `run.json` with `study_provenance`, one seed
  row), then runs the existing `verify --run <dir> --verify-dir <dir> --designs <hash>` body, so
  `designs/<hash>/{metrics.json,response.npz,mesh.msh,design.json}` exist and `#/run/<id>/3d` renders
  the design unchanged. The child owns the GPU lock (`HORNLAB_GPU_LOCK=refuse`, one CUDA solve at a
  time) and refuses - with a job reason and no run dir - when the lane is held, the design is
  unknown/unmeasured, or the study has no results or recorded config. `(study, design) -> run_id` is a
  small ledger beside the registry: no new artifact kind, no `studies/**` edit.
- Study page: a **Solves** table (Design -> `#/run/<id>/3d` once solved, plus a verify link; Kind, J,
  Physical, Outcome) with a per-row **Solve in 3D** and an explicit reason when disabled.
- Tests (19 new): `tests/test_gui_study_solves_view.py` (J order + missing-J last, bounded/truncated,
  physical-only units, missing artifact invents nothing, ledger link only while the run exists, active
  job) and `tests/test_gui_study_solve_design_job.py` (real standalone run dir, GPU-held refusal,
  unknown design, no results, unmeasured design, no recorded config, ledger link, duplicate submit
  reuses one run, server routing, panel exposure, a failed verify never advertises a finished run);

## 2026-11-16 (23:00) - A running BoTorch study was invisible in the shell; it is not any more

- Observed live: night `home18_a_2026-11-16` (runner started 22:09) ran `prep_a_turbo_ath14`
  (bayes-venv `prepare_study.py`, 22:25:54 -> 22:32:30, exit 0) and then `a_turbo_ath14`
  (`studies.cli run --execute`, started 22:32:30). A BoTorch study was executing while Home said
  **GPU Idle**, the lane panel said "not running - stale lock left by c1_core_law_wide_s2402", and
  the nav pill said "stopped search - no resumable run folder". Each line was true about *locks*;
  together they read as "nothing is running".
- Cause: every running surface keys off a lane lock or a `runs/<ts>-screen-*` folder. A study prep
  or run takes the GPU lock only **per solve**, so between solves it holds nothing, and a study is
  not a run folder. `/api/status` already shipped `queues[].open_step`; nothing rendered it as a
  headline and nothing linked it to the study.
- Fix: (a) Status and Home get a **"Running now - night <name>"** card naming the open step, its
  kind (BoTorch prep / BoTorch run / search / verify / diagnostics), elapsed time and the study it
  belongs to, with **Open the study live view**; (b) the sidebar gets one `NIGHT <step> - <kind>`
  line under the lane chips, so every page shows it; (c) the queue timeline marks only the **last**
  unclosed START as "running" - an earlier step with no END reads "no END line" (today
  `a_ext_v8_s1234` was shown as running for 30+ min after the runner reloaded the night file and
  moved on); (d) `server.py::_annotate_night_studies` resolves the step's `--root` to the study id
  and label, reading **that one registry** (a `list_studies` walk over all 17 roots pushed the
  Status first paint past 4 s; one root lookup is ~1 s cold).

  (BoTorch))`, "7.6m elapsed", the study label, and the link opens the study's Live tab with the KPI
  strip live ("Screens used / total 2 / 60", verify 0/6, refusals 0) while the run is in flight.

## 2026-11-15 (later) - Spiral pucker vs ATH radial ridge; wide radial-relief cell visible in GUI

- Research note: `docs/research/typologies/SPIRAL_PUCKER_VS_RADIAL_RIDGE_2026-11-15.md`.
  The rolled spiral's `pucker_*` is a z-only corrugation; its window saturates at 180 degrees
  and stays on through the 270-degree lip, so it bows the H/V faces forward and leaves a wavy
  rim. It is not ATH's radial ridge. The screenshot's `az_*` per-direction law is radial; the
  visible `b=1.2` / `amp=11.5` / `cos=-15` makes V dominant (CORE uses `b=0.618` / `amp=35`),
  which is why the vertical faces bow out. ATH Tritonia/CORE open the diagonal 7-10 degrees
  wider; the ridge is the integrated per-direction flare.
- The existing `rolled_family` radial mode pulls H/V inward and leaves the diagonal as a
  ridge. New shape-only cell `rf__rect_radial_wide_v7`: same spiral base, inward seed 12/16 mm,
  bounds 0-30 / 0-40 mm, window 0.50/0.80/0.96; mesh 541 x 299 x 241 mm, 5,096 DOF;
  `tests/test_rolled_family_geometry.py` 32 passed.
- GUI: added `examples/catalog.gui.yaml` entry and regenerated the parameter catalog
  (`param-catalog.v1.json`, `PARAMETERS.md`, `TYPOLOGIES.md`). The typology list now shows
  `rf__rect_radial_wide_v7` (enabled, 5 knobs); suggested starts 6/8 subtle, 12/16 clear,
  16/22 dramatic. The sandbox preview now resolves `rolled_family` through its canonical
  `resolve_grid` (the generic rows march rejected the `mode` key); verified `available:true`,
  `shape3d.available:true`, dims 535.7 x 294.7 x 235.1 mm. Hard-refresh and restart the GUI
  server (the preview fix is Python code).
- Evidence: `docs/renders/2026-11-15-pucker/` (six-view comparison, relief range sheet,

## 2026-11-13 (23:3xZ) - COMBINED SPEED CAMPAIGN DESIGNED (PIN x BATCHING FACTORIAL); THREE RECON LANES REPORTED

- **Why combined:** the owner wants to adopt more than G2 at once. A3 (skip the fused identity cache) and frequency
  batching (G1) both amortise *per-request* setup, and A3's per-request cache build is part of what batching would
  amortise - so sequential adoption double-counts the overlap. A factorial measures the interaction.
- **Design:** `docs/queue/SPEED_COMBINED_2026-11-13.md`; night files
  `docs/queue/speed_combo_2026-11-14_{oldpin,newpin}.yaml` (both `--dry-run` exit 0). Two blocks of four arms:
  `{batch 1, batch 12} x {p80x60__osse_ext_throat_700_v7, p80x60__ath_core_14in_700_v7}`, `--budget 1` so every arm
  solves the same seed geometry. Block 1 on pin `0850ef39` (current), block 2 after the swap to `9ec86b0`.
  Pre-declared rules: adopt a factor only at wall ratio <= 0.85, compare <= 0.039 dB / 1 deg, lower peak VRAM, zero
  shared spill. Budget ~45-55 GPU-minutes including the ceiling sweep.
- **Lane summary (three parallel recon lanes):** (1) every speed idea already documented, with status/measured
  gain/GPU cost/resolution flag; (2) the mesh state - C1 audit is the only landed mesh work, production defaults are
  untouched (`rear_res_factor 1.0`, `curvature_npts 0`), the mesher fork checkout is stale (at `b922e80`, the pinned
  `55da4f4` object is absent locally); (3) the per-frequency lifecycle - **the batching knob is not used in
  production** (`cma._prepare` never passes it; one request per frequency, so caches + `GC.gc(true)` + `cuda.reclaim()`
  recur per frequency), and the fused route also builds two dense **host** N x N identity matrices per request that it
  never reads (Lane C candidate B, a second A3-shaped patch).

  UI fidelity selector.

## 2026-11-03 (01:31Z) - BENCHMARK: CPU BEATS CUDA AT THE MEH MESH SIZE; 16 kHz RUNS ON CPU

- New `tools/bench/cpu_vs_cuda_meh.py` (15-minute budget, timestamped log + JSON). Measured on the owner's box,
  pin unchanged, 372 s total: `docs/evidence/BENCH_CPU_VS_CUDA_2026-11-03.md`, raw log in
  `runs/bench_cpu_cuda_20261103T013105Z/`.
- **A. CPU does multi-tag solves** (2-tag tetra, 1 kHz, 2.34 s). The MEH path is not CUDA-only.
- **B. Production T2 mesh (8,044 dofs, 2 tags), warm protocol (warm-up call, then the same 2-frequency call twice):**
  CUDA **37.2 s/frequency** (repeats 71.6 / 74.5 s for two frequencies, peak VRAM 7,853 MiB) vs CPU
  **5.86 s/frequency** (repeats 11.6 / 11.7 s). **CPU is 6.4x faster**; max |dSPL| 5.03e-04 dB. This is the same
  documented CUDA cliff: fast at ~6k dofs (the 12-frequency screen measured 3.6 s/frequency at 5,872 dofs), then
  collapse by ~8k.
- **C. 16 kHz on CPU.** The earlier 16 kHz failures were the application's dof cap (8,900), not the mesh or the
  card. With the cap raised for the diagnostic build: 49,757 triangles / **25,171 dofs**, built in 5.0 s, CPU
  solves 1 kHz in **100.7 s**. CUDA static storage for that mesh is **46.9 GiB** (audit formula 24.N.E + 32.N^2),
  so the 8 GB card cannot hold it. Wall caveat stands: at epw 5.4 the driven patches resolve to ~21.8 kHz but the
  rigid walls only to ~10.3 kHz.
- **Implication:** for the MEH's dof regime the CPU backend is the faster engine and needs no VRAM. The
  rent-a-GPU-first conclusion in the hardware audit should be revisited for screens specifically; a CPU screen may
  already be the cheap path, with the GPU reserved for what it actually wins.


## 2026-11-03 (02:00Z) - 40-DESIGN CUDA-vs-CPU SWEEP: NO SINGLE WINNER, CROSSOVER AT BOTH ENDS

- New `tools/bench/cuda_cpu_40designs.py`: **40 stored designs, no CAD/re-meshing** (30 single-source stratified
  across the dof range + 10 multi-entry with tag 10), one identical 1 kHz solve each per backend, hosts cleared
  between arms. Ran 358.6 s. Evidence: `docs/evidence/BENCH_40_DESIGNS_2026-11-03.md`, rows in
  `runs/bench_40designs_20261103T015652Z/`.
- **Result [measured]:** CUDA cold first call 26.5 s vs CPU 2.5 s; warm means 3.54 vs 4.18 s; sums over 40 designs
  164.4 s vs 165.5 s; median CPU/CUDA **2.23x**; CPU won **6/40**; SPL parity max **3.6e-05 dB**; CUDA peak VRAM
  7,841 MiB.
- **The crossover is a shape, not a point.** CPU faster below 1k dofs (0.17-0.22 s vs 0.35-0.72 s) and at
  8,472/8,530 dofs (18.1/18.9 s vs **41.6/53.6 s**); CUDA faster by 1.5-4x from 1k to ~7k dofs. The CUDA cliff is
  located sharply between 6,929 dofs (5.81 s) and 8,472 dofs (41.63 s) - 7x for +22 % dofs - while CPU scales
  smoothly.
- **Implication for screens:** stay on CUDA at 1-7k dofs, move to CPU above ~7k. Physics is backend-independent to
  3.6e-05 dB, so the choice is purely throughput. Caveat: one frequency, one design per dof value, and CPU cost is
  mesh-dependent.

  38.8-43.8 s/freq. `nvidia-smi` cannot see that. The "fresh host" resets were `taskkill /IM julia.exe`, a no-op
  for the worker_host tree. The 40-design bench had CUDA faster on 34/40 (median 2.2x). Full write-up and the
  withdrawn PR #19 conclusion: `docs/evidence/BENCH_AUDIT_2026-11-03.md`.

  LHS once, `assemble_burton_miller_rhs_cuda` per extra channel, one LU. Opt-in flag unchanged; single channel
  untouched; VENDORING.md entry. Julia MEH testset CUDA **16/16** (new fused-vs-four-operator per-channel check),
  CPU 7/7. **Pin bumped to `0850ef3`** (pyproject, TOOLCHAIN) - the fork branch must be pushed before this lands.

  headless request overlay with the exact frequency list (default 1/12 octave from 100 Hz, top capped at what the mesh resolves),
  `handoff.json` (mesh sha256, driven area, observation set-up, conventions) and `FOR_YOUR_FRIEND.md`. `solve` runs the high-res
  reference (existing `solve_spec` + backend; only the frequency list, angle count and balloon size replaced) on the full handoff
  mesh or, with `--symmetric`, on the reduced mesh; GPU lock, VRAM baseline, hosts cleared before and verified gone after.
  `import` reads Boundary Lab GUI text exports, the balloon folder, a headless run folder and generic CSV. `compare` aligns grids
  (copies only), derives on-axis / off-axis family / H and V maps / -6 dB beamwidth / DI (balloon) / balloon difference / phase /
  impedance, per-band max / RMS / median, PASS / WARN / FAIL against tolerances (starting points, not standards; override with
  JSON), a convention checker (6.02 dB, 3.01 dB, 12.04 dB, 60 dB, +-20 dB/decade drive-basis slope, time convention, polarity,
  delay, radius, mirrored angles, H/V swap, frequency-axis scale), and writes `report.html` (charts embedded; matplotlib PNG
  when installed, otherwise built-in SVG / PNG), `summary.json`, `verdict.txt`.
- **Boundary Lab formats: verified vs inferred** (static read of `JWSound/boundary-lab` `15f9a89`, 2026-11-02; details in the
  guide section 1). Verified in source: schema-10 project keys, preference names, frequency grid formula, polar arc geometry,
  Fibonacci balloon count rule, polar / on-axis / balloon export formats, headless run layout and quantity ids, phasor
  `exp(+i w t)`. **Found:** polar exports are normalized to the on-axis sample, balloon and polar exports are clipped to the SPL
  Min/Max preference, and **Normalized Channel Correction (default ON) flattens each channel on axis before export** (the project
  switches it off; the friend must confirm). BL `pyproject` now pins BEAT Engine 0.7.0 (our 2026-10-21 notes said 0.6.0).
  Inferred, unrun: that the GUI opens the generated project untouched, an impedance dock text export, RMS vs peak (3.01 dB).
- **Physics note that shapes the plan:** Hornfab drives unit ACCELERATION, BL 1 m/s VELOCITY: `+20 log10(2 pi f)` dB and a
  conjugate, done once in `compare/hornfab_side.py` and cross-checked against `solve/phasor.py` in tests. **The 8 GB card cannot
  solve a 20 kHz mesh** (`TOOLCHAIN.md` ceilings ~5.5k full / ~8.9k quarter dofs), so "full band" means "up to what the mesh
  resolves"; the export prints that limit and `solve --dry-run` the cost.

## 2026-11-01 - HARDWARE DECISION STUDY: RENTAL FIRST; FULL-WALL MESH IS MUCH LARGER

- Owner clarified this is a theoretical rent-versus-buy decision; no rental machines configured. Rental spend $0, no new BEM solves/screens. `docs/evidence/HARDWARE_2026-11-01.md` records the study, current published rates and explicitly conditional costs.
- Four CPU-only diagnostic builds on the fixed T2 seed: EPW 4.2 => 8,625 dofs / 16,909 triangles, global valid-to 6,015 Hz; EPW 6 => 17,211 / 33,938, global 8,583 Hz; EPW 8.4 => **33,959 / 67,245, global 12,009 Hz, valid**; EPW 9 => 38,819 / 76,919, global 12,864 Hz, valid. This is validator sizing, not acoustic convergence or a proven minimum over all geometries. Shipped configs untouched.
- Source audit of unchanged pin `1efdc6f`: standard CUDA uses fixed dense direct solves, repeating LHS/refactorization per channel; CPU/Metal GMRES cost model is not the CUDA route. At N=33,959/E=67,245 the concurrently live operators+identities+LHS alone require **85.410 GiB** before extra workspace. A 24/32 GB card is a coarse-mesh test candidate; the first requested full-wall discrete tier worth testing is H200 141 GB. No fit/runtime claim was measured on it.
- Historical NPZ/NDJSON extraction corrects the handoff's seed/winner attribution: T2 winner is N=5,872/E=11,456 with baseline/peak 513/7,575 MiB; T1 winner N=6,249/E=12,205 with baseline/peak 330/7,840 MiB. Across 69 successful historical screen candidates, assembly is the largest reported engine stage (~2 s/frequency, versus ~0.2 s solve). No 12 kHz throughput inference follows.
- Flat device-use peaks do not prove constant workspace; CUDA 719 does not uniquely establish OOM. Current `vram_41f.csv` differs from the earlier trace described in M8 and has no verified idle baseline. These refine the older capacity diagnosis; the recorded failures and prior screen winners remain unchanged.
- Shared-host multi-GPU work is not a one-line change: evaluator/persistence side effects, global lock, all-host cleanup and worker registry identity need isolation. Two separate single-GPU machines, one brief each, are a simpler future deployment test. All cross-card, unified-memory, lane-scaling and overnight measurements remain open. `doctor`: 11/11 checks passed; evidence excerpts checked against decoded bytes. No production code/pins/tolerances changed.

  gains, volumes, EQ and spl_max curves, inner_J, n_evals, seed), deterministic for a fixed seed, `ValueError` on
  hostile input.

## 2026-10-30 (16:00Z) - FIX: 3D EVOLUTION MESHES NO LONGER PUNCH RANDOM TRIANGLE HOLES

**What the owner saw.** On the evolution 3D time-lapse ("improvement frames only", run
`20261029T155433Z-screen-5b871c`) the horn looked like a mix of solid and fully transparent triangles,
with the shape dissolving into speckle at the silhouette.

**Root cause.** `data.evolution_frames3d` decimated above the per-frame cap by stride subsampling
(`tris[::k]`, `k = ceil(n_tris_full / cap)`). On a connected sheet that keeps every k-th triangle and
deletes the rest, so a k=2 frame lost ~half its faces as scattered single-triangle holes. The old cache
for that run held exactly that: 11.8k-16.6k-tri frames cut to ~5-6k.

**Fix (`hornlab_search/gui/data.py`).** New `_cluster_decimate` / `_cluster_once`: vertex-clustering
decimation (floor-snap vertices onto a grid, weld each occupied cell to its members' centroid, drop
degenerate and duplicate faces, compact unused vertices, bisect the grid size until the tri count sits
just under the cap). It coarsens the sheet but never punches per-triangle holes. Symmetry-plane vertices
(`'1'` -> x=0,y=0; `'14'` -> x=0; `'12'` -> y=0) are snapped to exactly zero so the mirrored seam has no
slit. The same path replaces `mesh_surface`'s `tris[:max_tris]` prefix truncation (additive
`decimated:true` key only when it fires). `M3D_DEFAULT_CAP` 6000 -> 30000 and `M3D_VERSION` 1 -> 2 (the
version is in the cache key, so every stale stride-decimated cache is invalidated). Real run: all 6
frames now undecimated, 11,816-16,636 tris x4 mirror = 47k-67k rendered triangles per frame.

**Verified.** `tests/test_gui_integration_phases.py` decimation test rewritten to the hole-free contract
(12x12 grid, 242 tris, cap 100): tri count <= cap, zero degenerate faces, symmetry vertices exactly 0.
`pytest tests/test_gui.py tests/test_gui_mesh_quadrants.py tests/test_gui_integration_phases.py
tests/test_gui_brief_authoring.py` = 131 passed; `compileall hornlab_search/gui` clean.

## 2026-10-29 (late) - FAST-BEM RESEARCH: QUADRATURE FIRST, GMRES SECOND, FMM AT 14K+ (zero GPU)

Owner-directed research pass. **Docs only: no code, config, example, test or D-night file touched; no GPU or
solver job run; nothing committed.** New report:
`docs/research/MATRIX_FREE_GPU_GMRES_FMM_2026-10-29.md` (also `NEXT_DEV_PRIORITIES` P13 and
`plan/12_RESEARCH_BASIS.md` section 18).

- **Verdict.** At 5-6k dofs the dense fused CUDA path is assembly-bound (73-96 % of per-frequency wall,
  `CAMPAIGN_SMOKE_2026-10-27.md:57`) and already one-matrix + device LU. Matrix-free/FMM is **not** the 2x at
  our current size. The cheapest credible 2x is quadrature order 4 -> 2. FMM is a feasibility play at 14k+ and
  the only path at 20k+. **No 10x is supported at 5-10k.**
- **The quadrature finding.** Order 4 = 6-point triangle rule = **36 point-pairs per element pair**; order 2 =
  3 points = **9 point-pairs** (`forks/hornlab-beat-bem/docs/beat-engine-CUDA.md:53`; `config.py:32,405`) -
  4x fewer kernel evaluations. The fork already has a wavelength-driven 1/2/4 selector with `kh` cutoffs
  (`q1_max=0`, `q2_max=2.0`; `BeatEngineDriver.jl:207-229`) but it is **CPU-only and discarded on CUDA**
  (`:186-187`, `:1766-1773`). At epw 6, `kh ~ 1.05` -> order 2.
- **CUDA has no GMRES.** The fused CUDA solve is `lu!` (`BeatEngineCudaBurtonMiller.jl:642-648`); the fork's
  GMRES (35-136 iterations, worst 549; FP64 Krylov because FP32 loses orthogonality 584-1000 vs 35-42) is
  CPU/Metal only (`BeatEngineDenseSolve.jl:14-55,363-372,72-73`). Expected gain on CUDA **1.0-1.4x**, plus a
  ~1.0-1.8 GB peak-VRAM saving from deleting the LU workspace [inferred] - a feasibility lever, not a 2x.
- **FMM** is 2-5x only at 14-20k, and even there the constants at kD ~ 100-235 are unverified. Exafmm-t is
  CPU/low-frequency/dormant; PVFMM is the GPU candidate but the BM layer is months; FMM3D `hfmm3d` is the best
  CPU algorithm fit; H-matrix/ACA ranks blow up at kD ~ 100. bempp-cl FMM is CPU Exafmm, not a GPU production
  path (`exafmm` is not even installed in `.venv`).
- **Axisymmetric/multimodal** is the only 10-100x (round horns, m=0, ~400 unknowns, ms/freq), does **not**
  apply to the 90x60/90x90 morph briefs, and stays WP13 owner-deferred.
- **Also recorded (gotchas found):** `CAMPAIGN_SMOKE`'s "iterative solve 0.07-0.94 s" is a dense LU on CUDA;
  `_cuda_use_matrix_free_burton_miller_rhs` is RHS-only (`BeatEngineCore.jl:1509,1528`); `gmres_tol` is hashed
  and recorded but never applied on Beat (`solve/beat.py:24-25`); an axisymmetric brief is not an axisymmetric
  BEM.
- **Next steps (owner sign-off for any fork change):** Phase 0 phase timing on 3 stored meshes x 3 freqs ->
  Phase 1 quadrature A/B (expose `solve.quadrature_order`, SPL <=0.05 dB at 500 Hz/2 kHz, <=0.10 dB at 8 kHz,
  bw <=0.3 deg, DI <=0.05 dB, >=1.5x at 5k or >=1.3x at 14k) -> Phase 2 GMRES on CUDA -> Phase 3 bempp
  FMM/OSRC CPU probe -> Phase 4 PVFMM/FMM3D only if justified.

## 2026-10-29 (04:05Z) - PLAN WRITTEN: CONE SOURCE MODEL (the rigid piston is the assumption)

Owner asked for a senior-level plan to fix the cone source after the research pass showed the directivity claim
is unearned above ~1 kHz. **Plan only, nothing implemented.** New doc
`docs/CONE_SOURCE_MODEL_PLAN_2026-10-29.md`; indexed, and elevated in `NEXT_DEV_PRIORITIES.md` as **P0b**
(it blocks every cone_plughorn directivity claim).

- **The finding.** The cone face (tag 2) is driven as a rigid axial piston at all frequencies. A 10-inch paper
  cone is pistonic only to its first break-up, ~0.7–1.5 kHz [consensus; must be measured]; the band is
  220 Hz–4 kHz. Since `p(θ) âˆ ∫ v(r)J₀(k r sinθ) r dr`, sign changes in `v(r)` must produce lobes/nulls a
  uniform piston cannot. So 1–4 kHz pattern/DI is geometry-only today. The BEM geometry is fine; the boundary
  condition on the cone is the assumption.
- **Code audit recorded in the plan** (all verified this pass): beat `SolveConfig.source_tag` asserts exactly
  ONE source tag (`((tag, _),) = velocity_sources.items()`); `source_profile_alpha` is a per-face J0 factor,
  **fused-CUDA only**, refused in both Python and Julia; `julia/BeatEngineDriver.jl::source_profile_factors`
  (~841) is the seam to generalise; `sweep.py` computes the entry impedance from the **mean** pressure over the
  source tag (must become velocity-weighted); `solve/bempp.py` drives uniformly
  (`velocity_sources={SOURCE_TAG: 1.0}`) so the CPU cross-check cannot see a profile yet; STEP labels are
  pinned to `{driver, wall}` with exactly one driver face (`multicell.LABELS`, `read_face_inventory`), so
  ring tags are a schema + mesher + `_is_driver_face` change.
- **Recommended route.** C0 honesty now (retire `Sd_eff` as a directivity model, print the piston-valid band);
  C1 `SourceProfile` data model + validation; C2 beat CPU factors + the generalised Julia builder; C3 bempp so
  the profile is cross-checked; C4 `A_eq` + velocity-weighted `Z_rad` in `resp.meta`, `drive()` consumes them;
  C5 provenance/reporting; C6 measured LDV/accelerometer profile; C7 multi-tag rings only with evidence.
  Uniform profile must be byte-identical to today.
- **Two-way coupling is the trap** the plan calls out: the circuit must see the radiation impedance of the
  actual velocity distribution (`Z_rad = Î£ conj(v)pA / Î£|v|Â²A`), not the uniform mean, or level/impedance/
  excursion are inconsistent with the polars near break-up.
- **Research record** (sources + labels) is in the plan: Frankort 1975; Kagawa 1980; Hu 2017; Smith 1953
  (front chamber); Dodd 2008/09, Bernland 2019, Berggren 2020 (phase-plug wavefront); Morse & Ingard, Pierce,
  Williams (waveguide mode filtering, Rayleigh/Hankel); Keele 1975/77, Kolbrek 2008 (cutoff); Beranek/Olson;
  Hornresp/AkAbak/ABEC/COMSOL practice. **No published `Sd_eff(f)` law exists**; no measured cone-horn vs
  compression-horn polar comparison below cutoff was found.
- **Owner decisions listed:** approve C0; approve C1â€“C2; pick the driver; LDV access (or accept the 3â€“5
  accelerometer fallback); C7 now or later. No GPU, no solver, no code touched.

## 2026-10-27 (gcurve follow-up) - THE GUIDING CURVE NOW SITS AT THE MOUTH (`dist 1.0`), T0 VALID

- **Supersedes the width-130 workaround below.** That seed was valid (367 x 292, J 6.289) but it
  changed the intended mouth scale to pull the envelope back. The real defect was the curve
  **station**: at `gcurve_dist 0.5` the 335 mm outline sat halfway down the horn and the flare kept
  growing to the mouth (783 x 581 mm). At **`gcurve_dist 1.0` the outline is the mouth**, so width
  335 is the mouth width again. Box change: `gcurve_dist` hi 0.9 -> 1.0; the width box returns to
  the campaign 0.3-1.1x335 = 100.5-368.5 mm (39-143 was the workaround's box). `families.KeySpec`
  has no lo/hi clamp on `gcurve_dist`, and the mesher's own formula accepts `0 < dist <= 1.0` as a
  fraction of L, so 1.0 is allowed. The cell header now explains the station fix and both attempts.
- **Measured geometry:** dry-run bbox 0.1676 x 0.1457 m after the quarter mirror -> full mouth
  **335.2 x 291.5 mm**, depth 146 mm, inside the 380 x 300 brief envelope.
- **T0, budget 1, screen:** `seed J = 9.85253`, **1,855 dofs**, 3,543 triangles, 1 new / 0 cached,
  7.1 s/candidate, objective v3. The v3 dataset record landed (`dataset/shard-0030.jsonl`).

  control seed 15.045, but it is **worse** than the width-130 workaround (6.289) and the crease seed

  control runs 1.15, so it is not a clean A/B. The guiding curve still needs a real T1/diagonal
  check before any ranking claim.

## 2026-10-26 (night, during the smoke run) - READ-ONLY RUN OBSERVER (`tools/observe_run.py`)

- **Why:** the first pass at "can we run twice as fast" had to infer the GPU/CPU phase split from
  ndjson timestamps. This records it directly, once per 5 s, for any night: GPU utilisation, VRAM
  used/total, power, temperature, SM clock vs max, total CPU % and the per-process CPU of
  `python.exe` / `julia.exe` / `hornlab-search.exe`, the running job (newest job log), and the
  newest run's eval count, last row's mesh/solve seconds, dof count and error kind. One JSON line
  per sample to `runs/nights/<night>/observe.ndjson`; on exit it writes
  `observe_summary.md` (phase shares, utilisation histogram, VRAM/power stats).
- **Read-only by construction:** `nvidia-smi` queries, `psutil` counters, and reads of
  `summary.jsonl` / the newest job log / the newest `search.ndjson`. It never launches a solver and
  never writes into a run directory.
- **First samples (smoke_2026-10-27, `t1__b3bt__salmon_x_signed`):** GPU 100 % util at 695 MiB VRAM
  of 8,188, 77 W, 70 degC, SM clock 2,550 of a 3,105 MHz max, total CPU 22.6 % while `python.exe`
  is 128 % and `julia.exe` 144 % - the mesh/metrics side uses ~2.7 cores while most cores idle.
  That is the pipelining headroom the speed-up analysis was looking for.
- **How to use it later:** phase shares give the CPU/GPU pipeline ceiling (`1 / gpu_solve_share`);
  the utilisation histogram gives the concurrency headroom; `evals` deltas vs dofs give a
  throughput model; the VRAM column gives the two-way-parallel budget per cell size.
- Docs + one tool; no code path the campaign uses was touched.

## 2026-10-26 (night, latest) - PER-DIRECTION OSSE LAW: ATH CORE's a(p)/n(p)/s(p) as searchable knobs

- **Why:** the CORE/TwinRay creases are not a guiding curve and not Morph alone - the published script (at-horns.eu/core.html) writes the wall angle and the termination as expressions of the azimuth: `a(p) = a_deg + az_a_sf_amp*SF(p) + az_a_cos_amp*|cos p|^az_a_cos_pow`, `n(p) = n + az_n_cos2_amp*cos^2 p`, `s(p) = s + az_s_cos2_amp*cos^2 p`, with the Gielis superformula `SF(p) = (|cos(m p/4)/a|^n2 + |sin(m p/4)/b|^n3)^(-1/n1)`. Every previous typology used one coverage angle (the constant-azimuth reduction), so no shape in the tree could crease on the diagonals.
- **What landed (`design/families.py`):** 11 `az_*` knobs (section `azlaw`) on native OSSE, `AZLAW_DEFAULTS`, `azlaw_expressions` / `azlaw_values`, and `to_mesher_config` folding them into the mesher's OWN p-expressions for `profile.a_deg` / `profile.n` / `profile.s` (the `az_*` names never reach the mesher; the emitted a-expression falls back to the numeric base when `a_deg` is absent). Validation refuses a non-multiple-of-4 `az_sf_m` (quarter-model mirror symmetry), any sampled `a(p)` outside (0.5, 89.5) deg (every 3 deg over the quarter), and `n(p) <= 0` while `s != 0`; each refusal names the knob that caused it. **Absent or zero = byte-identical:** `json.dumps(sort_keys=True)` of the mesher config equals the no-az-keys call and carries no `az_` token anywhere.
- **Measured (the published recipe reproduces):** CORE values (a_deg 5, amp 35, m 4, n1 12, n2 15, n3 16, a 1, b 0.618, cos amp -15 pow 10, n 6 + 1.5 cos^2, s 0.6 + 0.23 cos^2) give **a = 25.0 / 33.8 / 23.4 deg at p = 0 / 45 / 90**, n 7.5 / 6.0, s 0.83 / 0.60 - the H/V numbers match the earlier `ath_core` midpoints exactly, and the diagonals open ~9 deg wider.
- **Sandbox (`gui/static/sandbox.js`):** a "Per-direction law (Ath CORE)" card on every OSSE typology (11 sliders + a CORE preset + a "crease this horn" preset that moves `a_deg` so `a(0)` is unchanged). **Committed unverified in a browser** (owner: no GUI click-testing tonight) - an owner eyes-on item, not a test result.
- **Docs:** `docs/research/typologies/ATH_CORE_TWINRAY_MORPH_2026-10-25.md` gains section "5b. Per-direction law (the exact CORE construction)" with the published expressions and the measured table.
- **Tests:** new `tests/test_design_azlaw.py` (6): the published a/n/s table, byte-inequality-free absence (no `az_` token anywhere), `az_sf_m 6` refused by name, `a(p) <= 0.5` refused, the folded expression in `profile.a_deg`, and the expression still emitted when the base key is absent. Focused gate **125 passed / 0 failed / 0 errors / 0 skipped** (`tests/test_design_azlaw.py`, `test_design_families.py`, `test_param_catalog.py`, `test_typology_ath_morph.py`, `test_design_generators_grid_variants.py`); `tools/gen_param_catalog.py --check` **OK** with **no regeneration needed** (the generator scans `examples/typologies/*.yaml`, and no committed typology carries `az_*` - the `az_*` knob docs are in `knobs_native.py` and reach the wire only for configs that use them); `node --check sandbox.js` **OK**.

## 2026-10-26 (night) - WHY NO ATH-STYLE CREASES, AND THE FIX: the OS-SE guiding curve in the sandbox

- **Owner question:** none of our typologies (incl. the TwinRay / CORE reconstructions) ever showed the puckered, lofted ridges of at-horns.eu's CORE / TwinRay / Opus; Morph was expected to make them and does not.
- **Diagnosis:** the creases come from a coverage angle that changes with DIRECTION around the axis. Ath gets it from the OS-SE **guiding curve** (superellipse / superformula, CORE's `sf()` script) and per-azimuth `a(p)` expressions; Morph only pulls the mouth outline to a rectangle. Our `ath_core` uses one coverage angle (the constant-azimuth reduction), `ath_twinray_380` is a FREEFORM generator with only H/V profiles, and NO config ever set a guiding curve although the search layer already carries `gcurve_*` (OSSE only) and the mesher supports it. Measured: CORE's mouth radius is 198 mm at every angle; with a pinched superformula curve (m1=m2=4, n1=0.5, n2=n3=1) it swings 407 -> 212 mm with azimuth, and with CORE's rectangle Morph the walls fold into throat-to-corner creases (seen in the sandbox 3D).
- **Sandbox:** a Guiding-curve card on every OSSE typology (off / superellipse / superformula; width, height/width, position along the length, rotation, se_n, sf a/b/m1/m2/n1/n2/n3; presets pinched 4-lobe / diamond / soft square / rectangle; per-knob 'search' ticks saved as search rows like Morph). The mesher requires a circular cross-section with a guiding curve, so the card holds exponent 2 / aspect 1 while it is on. A TwinRay-like OSSE (L 192, a 35, a0 5, pinched curve, rectangle Morph 380x303) previews at 383 x 306 x 188 mm vs the published 380 x 303 x 192.

## 2026-10-26 (campaign Phase 0) - `generator.seed_policy` opt-out LANDED (impl-code1; absent = byte-identical)

- **Why:** `_derive_generator_geometry` overwrites generator seeds from `target.f0_hz` on every campaign brief. Its rows constants are wrong for Salmon (1.88e5 vs measured 3.23e5 at stop 150) and its JMLC rule (geometric-mean mouth then fc-floor clamp) collapses Le Cleac'h seeds to ~313 mm round horns. The campaign needs hand-measured seeds without disabling the honest K-law feasibility record.
- **Contract:** new optional `generator.seed_policy`, value `derive` (default; absent behaves exactly as today) or `explicit`. With `explicit`, `_derive_generator_geometry` returns before touching `seed_params` or `bounds`, keeps the feasibility block, and appends `{"knob": "-", "note": "seed_policy explicit: derivation skipped"}`. Anything else is a `ConfigError` naming `generator.seed_policy`. The directive stays in `raw` (so `config_sha` covers it) but is filtered out of `Config.generator` and defensively stripped in `registry.materialize`, so it can never reach a mesher config.
- **Byte-identity:** `tests/test_config_seed_policy.py` pins the pre-change goldens for `salmon_elliptical` and `lecleach_rollback` under `examples/briefs/organic_rollback_14in.yaml` (seed_params, derivation notes, `config_sha` `9b5cc34de453` / `f2e29be7c418`); explicit keeps every YAML seed/bound and refuses bad values; a materializer spy proves the key is never passed through.
- **Verification:** focused 10/10, adjacent config/derivation/design 90/90; standard gate green - compileall, catalog `--check`, `node --check` x8, offline suite **1626/0/0/0** (`runs/step2a/suite.xml`; 1607 baseline + 10 new + 9 from a concurrently-added untracked lane file, never staged). No GPU/Julia work.

## 2026-10-26 - MEASURED GPU CEILING AT 8 kHz AND 10 kHz (owner-requested stress ladder; real VRAM numbers replace the earlier estimates)

- **Owner ask:** "what about 8,000 hertz - can we do that? why don't you run a test and see if it crashes my card", then "if we can actually fit it at 10,000 it's not going to crash the car". Also: cap the mouth at 500 mm and use whatever dispersion that supports.
- **Method (one GPU job at a time, repo hygiene followed):** pure-OSSE seeds (`s=0, k=1, aspect=1` so the analytic L->mouth relation is exact), `epw 6`, quarter domain, dof caps set to 200,000 so the PHYSICAL limit is what shows; each rung meshes, then solves ONE frequency at the ladder's top; `BeatBackend(track_vram=True)` reports peak; `worker.shutdown()` after each rung; Julia cleared before and after. Harness `%TEMP%\opencode\pass40\rung_test.py` (parameterised by band top); raw results in `rungs\8k|ladder.json` and `rungs\10k\ladder.json`.
- **8 kHz ladder (mouth / tris / solve / peak VRAM / headroom of 8,188 MB):**
  293 mm / 4,208 / 31.9 s / **1,219 MB** / 6,969 Â· 353 / 5,972 / 28.7 s / **2,193** / 5,995 Â· 403 / 7,644 / 29.5 s / **3,340** / 4,848 Â· 474 / 10,402 / 29.4 s / **5,797** / 2,391 Â· 500 / 11,516 / 29.7 s / **7,212** / 976 Â· 550 / 13,866 / 24.7 s / 7,397 / 791 Â· 635 / 18,236 / 25.3 s / 7,501 / 687.
- **10 kHz ladder:**
  293 / 6,476 / 21.6 s / **2,541** / 5,647 Â· 353 / 9,232 / 29.1 s / **4,853** / 3,335 Â· 403 / 11,816 / 30.9 s / **7,333** / 855 Â· 424 / 13,060 / 31.0 s / 7,545 / 643 Â· 448 / 14,428 / 35.4 s / 7,330 / 858 Â· 474 / 16,068 / 64.0 s / 7,516 / 672 Â· 500 / 17,832 / 25.6 s / 7,442 / 746.
- **No crash - confirmed, and the failure mode is understood.** The card never died; at the top rungs the peaks PLATEAU at ~7.3-7.5 GB (the physical 8,188 MB limit) and stderr carries `RuntimeError: Out of GPU memory trying to allocate ~630-660 MiB / Effective GPU memory usage: 100.00% (7.996 GiB)` with `Memory pool usage: 15.9 GiB reserved`. That pool figure is the giveaway: BEAT is oversubscribing past VRAM into host memory (WDDM), which is why a 474 mm 10 kHz solve still "completes" while taking 64 s instead of 31 s. **So "ok" is not "fits"** - the usable rule is PEAK + ~800 MB headroom (the GUI baseline alone is ~350-500 MB), not "did the solve return".
- **Verdict (the numbers that govern future briefs):**
  - **8 kHz: safe to ~474 mm** (5.8 GB, 2.4 GB headroom). 500 mm works but leaves under 1 GB - too tight for a long search. >=550 mm is memory-saturated and must be treated as unavailable.
  - **10 kHz: safe to ~353 mm** (4.9 GB, 3.3 GB headroom). 403 mm is the edge (7.3 GB, 855 MB); >=424 mm is saturated. 500 mm at 10 kHz is not viable.
  - Converting to dofs (measured tris x 0.51): 8 kHz safe ~5,300 dofs; 10 kHz safe ~4,700 dofs, edge ~6,000. **The shipped 5,000-dof screen cap and 8,900 verify cap were therefore well-judged** - this ladder says the physical ceiling is not far above them.
- **Owner brief set as of 2026-10-26 (saved in `examples/briefs/user/`):**
  - `cap500_90x90_650hz_1p4in` - 90x90 at **f0 650** (owner corrected 565 -> 650), mouth 434.2 mm inside the 500 mm cap. ~8.2k tris / ~4 GB at 8 kHz: the comfortable one.
  - `cap500_90x60_850hz_1p4in` - 90x60 at f0 850 (a 90x60 pattern at a 500 mm mouth requires >=847 Hz), mouth 332 x 498 mm.
  - `cap500_60x40_1270hz_1in` - the cap-compliant narrow brief: 40 deg at 500 mm requires >=1270 Hz, mouth 333 x 500 mm.
  - `narrow_60x40_800hz_1in` - **owner override, cap deliberately not applied**: 60x40 down to **800 Hz** needs 529.2 x 793.8 mm. At an 8 kHz top that extrapolates to ~28-29k tris, well past the 8,188 MB card; the owner accepted that it may fail ("it's gonna run on my card"). At a ~4 kHz top it is ~7.3k tris / ~3 GB and viable.
  - `wide_90x60_500hz_1p4in` (f0 500, 564 x 847 mm) stays as the unconstrained wide reference; `lecleach_90x90_1200hz_1in` (235 mm) stays as the Le Cleac'h brief.
  - Deleted as superseded: `cap500_100x100_500hz_1p4in` (owner: too wide), `cap500_90x90_565hz_1p4in` (f0 moved to 650), `narrow_60x40_880hz_1in` (replaced by the 800 Hz narrow).
- **Practical home:** the 434-500 mm briefs run best at a 5,500-6,000 Hz screen (~3.2-4 GB) with an 8 kHz verify on finalists; 10 kHz is only reachable at <=353 mm (measured).
- **Correction on record:** my earlier "a 500 Hz horn analysable to 10 kHz must be >=150-180 deg wide" line was arithmetic from forcing the mesh budget, not acoustics; a 500 mm mouth is 14.6 wavelengths at 8 kHz and cannot hold a 100 deg pattern there, let alone 180. The measured ladder supersedes that reasoning - the constraint is VRAM, and the honest fix is band-limiting what `cov` scores, not widening the horn into an impossible shape.
- **Follow-ups this unlocks:** (1) set `solve.cuda_fused: true` + `dof_cap_verify: 12000` for the 500 mm briefs since fused CUDA is the shipped path to the 12,000 caps; (2) add `target.cov_band_hz` so coverage is scored over the band the horn can actually hold while ripple/flat/DI score to 8-10 kHz; (3) the cap-500 briefs' dispersion table (f0 vs max coverage at 500 mm): 500 Hz -> 101.6 deg, 700 -> 72.6, 850 -> 59.8, 1000 -> 50.8, 1270 -> 40.0, 1450 -> 35.0.

## 2026-10-25 (late) - OWNER SCREENSHOT PASS: mouth ring mirrored, evolution 3D un-clipped, rollback section order preserved (three real bugs, each root-caused before editing)

- **What the owner saw** (two screenshots): the Front view drew the mouth as a single quarter fan anchored at the origin instead of a closed outline; the evolution time-lapse's 3D panel was completely blank (render chip and "mesh decimated to 15856 tris" both present, zero geometry); and the sandbox's vertical-plane section was a striped fringe instead of a wall band. The same mouth bug appeared on both pages, so it was one defect seen twice.
- **Fix 1 - mouth ring never mirrored** (`charts.js::mirrorRing`, new pure helper; wired into `evolution.js::mouthPath` and `sandbox.js::mouthBandPath` + the inner-ring stroke). Both pages received a symmetry-reduced ring from the payload and drew it verbatim, so a quarter payload rendered as one quadrant. The helper decides from the points themselves (the frames payload does not always carry `quadrants`): an arc inside one quadrant is mirrored into all four with traversal order preserved, a ring spanning one axis is mirrored across that axis, and a ring already spanning both axes is returned untouched (so full-ring/half payloads are never double-drawn).
- **Fix 2 - evolution 3D blank = a unit mismatch, not a renderer failure** (`view3d.js::init3dFrames`). Frame vertices are millimetres and `buildGeo` scales each geometry by 0.001 onto the metre stage, but the camera rig, lights and shadow ground were derived from the UNSCALED mm bounds: the horn occupied ~0.4 units while the camera sat ~600 units away with `near 0.001 / far 100`, so everything was beyond the far plane. The rig now computes its centre and `maxDim` in metres (`CENTRE_SCALE`), matching the geometry and matching `init3d`'s existing metre convention; the shadow-ground line already used `u.y0 * 0.001`, which is what exposed the inconsistency. `prepareFrames` is untouched, so the existing frame-preparation pins still hold.
- **Fix 3 - striped vertical plane = an invalid sort** (`sandbox.js::combinedSectionLoop`). The builder z-sorted `outer` ascending and `inner` descending to close the band loop, which is only valid for monotone meridians. Rollback rows typologies (`salmon_elliptical` at `g_stop_deg` 150 - the config in the screenshot) fold BACK in z near the mouth, so sorting scrambled the polygon and the even-odd fill broke into horizontal strips. The loop now preserves each plane's own point order (outer as given, inner reversed) and closes normally, which is valid for monotone and rollback meridians alike.
- **Verification:** `node --check` on charts.js / evolution.js / sandbox.js / view3d.js / app.js all green; `tests/test_gui_sandbox_page.py` + `test_gui_evolution_3d_toggle.py` + `test_gui_brief_authoring.py` + `test_gui.py` + `test_gui_param_tips.py` all pass. New pins in the sandbox node suite: a quarter ring must reach the -x and -y quadrants (mouth fix) and a non-monotone rollback meridian must come out in its original order, asserted exactly (sort fix).
- **Owner eyes-on:** reload the GUI (`tools/launch_gui.ps1`) and check the three views - the evolution 3D horn should now be visible and hittable with the camera/orbit, and both front views should show a closed mouth outline instead of a fan.

## 2026-10-25 (evening) - EVOLUTION 3D TOGGLE FIXED (fix-2 lane; branch `unified-typologies` @ cd71c1c; docs wording refreshed here)

- **The owner-visible bug:** ticking `3D` on the search time-lapse page left the canvas showing `3D off - flip the 3D toggle above.` while the checkbox rendered checked.
- **Root cause (as diagnosed in the entry below):** duplicate DOM id - the checkbox and the 3D container BOTH carried `id="evo-3d"`, so `getElementById` at the build/disable sites resolved the `<input>`; `init3dFrames` appended its WebGL canvas into a checkbox, the visible div kept the template placeholder, and `container._dispose3d` landed on the input while `data-v3d` sat on the div - so `route()`'s disposal sweep never disposed the player (context/rAF leak on navigation).
- **The fix (evolution.js +8/-2, no view3d.js change):** the CHECKBOX was renamed to `evo-3d-toggle`, keeping the container as `evo-3d`. Deliberate deviation from the diagnose-then-rename-the-container wording, and justified on record: an existing source pin (`tests/test_gui_brief_authoring.py:867`) pins the container markup as `id="evo-3d" data-v3d`; renaming the container would have forced edits to a green test, while renaming the checkbox achieves the identical unique-id fix with a smaller diff and zero pin churn. `build3d`/`disable3d` now genuinely resolve the `data-v3d` div (the marker element IS the player/disposal node, so the sweep disposes the real scene); the box state is coherent (starts unchecked matching the renderer, `disable3d` unchecks it again and restores the placeholder to the container); both directions of the improvements-only rule are untouched (`mode==="all"` forces 3D off; `enable3d()` forces `mode="best"`); the placeholder remains the genuine off-state text on the container only. `init3d`'s two other callers (`app.js` run-detail + 3D page) verified untouched.
- **Regression pin (new file `tests/test_gui_evolution_3d_toggle.py`, 4 tests):** source pins chosen over a node import because `evolution.js` is a browser ES module needing `document`/`fetch`/`CSS.escape` with no DOM shim in this env (the repo already pins evolution wiring this way). Asserts the two ids differ + exactly one `data-v3d` tag on the container; the player node is the marked node; the container id is never read as a checkbox and vice versa; box starts unchecked, placeholder appears exactly twice (template + restore), both rule directions present. **Negative control verified:** reverting only the checkbox id fails 3 of 4 tests.
- **Verification (pasted by the lane):** new test 4/4 (junit errors=0 failures=0) + the full GUI trio `test_gui.py`/`test_gui_brief_authoring.py`/`test_gui_integration_phases.py` 107/0/0/0 untouched + `node --check` evolution.js and view3d.js green + `compileall hornlab_search/gui/` green.
- **Residual eyes-on item (WebGL cannot render headlessly):** open `#/run/<id>/evolution`, tick 3D -> canvas visible inside the bordered box with the note "N improvement frames in 3D...", untick -> placeholder restored + box unchecked, switch to "every candidate" -> 3D turns off with its disclosure, navigate away/back a few times -> no rAF/WebGL growth. The pins prove the canvas lands in the right node and the placeholder cycles; three.js painting itself remains the owner's visual confirm.
- **Docs carried in this commit:** the plan entry below still described the checkbox as `evo-3d` (true at diagnosis time); this entry is now the record of the landed state.

Small isolated fix, queued as the first lane on the new branch.

- **Status-card Stop (designer lane):** the current-run card on `#/status` gains the Stop affordance with a three-state ownership rule (`stopAffordanceFor` â€” pure, node-tested over 12 cases): (1) GUI-started GPU job running â†’ two-step armed danger button (`â–  Stop` â†’ `Confirm stop`, auto-disarm 5 s; no browser `confirm()` â€” stated pattern) firing the committed `POST /api/job/<id>/cancel`, post-action line "stop requested â€” the run dir records the stopâ€¦"; (2) gpu lock held by an EXTERNAL process â†’ informational pill naming the lock pid ("run started outside the GUI (terminal) â€” the GUI only stops its own jobs"), never a button; (3) nothing running â†’ nothing rendered. One-GPU-at-a-time makes "newest running GUI GPU job" unambiguous; multiple disclose it. Launch rows keep their existing cancel (retitled `Stop run`). Startup-window honesty: GUI job running but no run folder yet â†’ minimal card with the button ("no run folder written yet") instead of a blinking-out control.

- **Resume plumbing (fixer lane, `gui/jobs.py` â€” verified against the CLI contract on disk):** the CLI's `--resume` takes a **DIRECTORY** (`metavar="DIR"` â€” a bare flag is refused), so the GUI `search` job kind gains an optional `resume: <run_id>` arg resolved via `_run_id` â†’ `search --resume <abs runs/<id>>` (config optional on resume: the CLI reuses `<run>/config.yaml`, so a config edited after the stop can't poison replay unless `--allow-config-change` is explicitly passed; `budget` omitted â†’ the run's own `cfg.search.budget`; **budget is a per-invocation NEW-eval cap, not auto-remaining** â€” disclosed to the owner in the contract update; `mode` omitted â†’ CLI default `screen` which REWRITES run.json mode â€” the UI passes the run's recorded mode). GPU kind, one-GPU lock, gpu-busy refusal, cancel, past-jobs reload all inherited (ordinary search job). Resumable markers on disk: `run.json status` `"running"` (stale after a GUI hard-stop â€” no `"stopped"` value exists in the writer) / `"interrupted"`; `"finished"` â†’ deliberate budget top-ups only; `"aborted"` retryable.
- **Honesty engineering:** Resume id sourcing from the stopped job's own `log_tail` (`runs/<id>` lines) validated against `/api/runs` summaries (exists + `budget == null || n < budget` â€” an exhausted run is finished; top-ups stay an owner action, never a pill side-effect); every resume runs `POST /api/preview` FIRST (server-side validation, zero side effects) and the confirm click is **blocked** if the previewed argv lacks `--resume*` ("â€¦would start a FRESH search, not a resume; nothing was started") â€” the pill's degrade ladder (missing run folder, exhausted budget, refused preview, launch error) always shows the real reason and re-arms. ## 2026-10-23 (local, ~14:30 EDT) - dead-worker-host recovery fixed (root cause found); `verify --brief` bug fixed; 12 kHz briefs

- **Root cause of the OSSE seed-4101 cascade (03:58)**: after the host died, `hornlab_beat_bem.worker.get_worker` kept handing out the SAME cached `HostedBeatWorker`, whose `submit` releases its slot on a send error but keeps the dead socket in `_connection`; our `recover_after_failure` killed hosts and marked cold but never dropped that client, so all 21 later candidates failed in ~1 s with `ConnectionResetError` at `BeatSolveSession(...)` (row tracebacks, `worker_client.py:122`). Fix (our layer only, no library edit): recovery calls `detach_workers` first (empties the library cache); `BeatBackend._solve` re-warms and retries a `worker_exit` candidate once (OOM / other not retried); `search` raises `SolverUnhealthyError` after 3 consecutive non-cached `solve_failed` -> run `aborted`, resumable (`solve_failed` rows are never memoised, so `--resume` re-solves them); a campaign records that entry as a failed job. Why the host died is still unknown (GPU rule 7).
- **Surrogate labels**: `to_training_arrays` drops `solve_failed` records (solver crash, not the design) and reports `meta.skipped_solve_failed`; deterministic failures stay as validity labels.
- **Bug: `verify --brief` was parsed and ignored** (same class as the 2026-10-22 search bug); a 12 kHz verify would have silently re-solved at 5.5 kHz. Now applied; with `--brief` the results go to a new run dir `runs/<ts>-verify-<id>` (config/run.json with `verify_of`/ndjson/best.json; the GUI lists it), without it the old `run/verify/` behaviour.
- New VERIFY-only briefs `examples/briefs/axi_90x90_1in_12k.yaml`, `hifi_90x60_1in_12k.yaml` (copies, `band_hi_hz: 12000`, P2 comment + cross-mode caveat); verify grid 300-12,000 Hz, 25 points, config verify dof cap (7,000) unchanged.
- The overnight queue's later sculpt seeds (new subprocess per seed) import these modules; each edit was compile-checked before saving and only failure paths change.
- `tests/test_report_html.py` zero-success test: setup now expects the resumable stop (3 failure rows instead of 10); its assertions are unchanged plus one on the row count.
- Offline suite: **808 passed, 18 deselected, exit 0**.

## 2026-10-23 (local, ~04:15 EDT) - local web GUI built; GPU-lock liveness bug found and fixed (queue untouched)

- **Bug (serious, fixed):** `gpulock._pid_alive` used `os.kill(pid, 0)`; on Windows signal 0 is CTRL_C_EVENT, so for a lock holder in another console it raised and the live holder looked STALE: a second GPU job from any other terminal would have taken over the lock, and `gpu-clean` would have killed the queue's julia mid-solve. Found because the new GUI showed the running queue as "stale". Now `OpenProcess` + `GetExitCodeProcess` (sends nothing). Verified: queue search pid 4916 alive=True and still writing rows; tests `tests/test_search_gpulock_pid.py` (incl. a guard that `os.kill` is never called on Windows). The running queue step loaded the old module but never re-checks the lock; the next steps import the fix.
- **GUI** (`docs/GUI_PLAN.md`, `hornlab-search gui`, http://127.0.0.1:8765): stdlib server + vanilla JS, no build step; views status / campaigns / runs / run detail (curves, polar maps, sensitivity, pinned bounds) / compare / briefs (save NEW user briefs only, validated with `load_brief`) / launch (allow-listed CLI argv, GPU-busy refusal) / 3D (three.js CDN, quarter mesh mirrored, 2D fallback).
